review.assessment: The change introduces `checkout/pricing.py`, implementing sequential discount application that correctly compounds percentages. This explains why an order of $100.00 with 20% and 10% codes results in a payable amount of $72.00 rather than the customer's additive expectation of $70.00; compounding discounts sequentially is mathematically standard and aligns with typical business logic when percentages are applied one after another. `MAX_TOTAL_PCT` is defined at module level but never enforced or referenced within `payable`, leaving total discount percentage validation to other parts of the system. The function uses floor division at each step (`// 100`), which consistently rounds down the discount amount per iteration and favors the merchant over a single-pass calculation; without access to `docs/discounts.md`, I cannot verify whether this rounding behavior or the lack of explicit cap enforcement matches the required specification. All provided structural, acceptance, and veto checks pass cleanly.
